title: Netflix Cancels Will Ferrell’s The Hawk After One Season
excerpt: Netflix has declined to renew Will Ferrell’s golf comedy The Hawk. The series reached No. 2 on the global English-language chart but reportedly carried substantial production costs.
seo_title: Netflix Cancels The Hawk After One Season
seo_description: Will Ferrell’s golf comedy ends after one season despite a global top-ten run. Here is what the report says about viewership, costs and his other projects.
body_md:
Netflix has decided not to order a second season of The Hawk, the golf comedy starring Will Ferrell. The cancellation was reported on November 25, 2026, more than four months after its July 16 premiere. Ferrell helped create the project and served as an executive producer in addition to playing its central character. It represented his first leading role in a television series.

## A respectable audience, but a costly production

Deadline reports that The Hawk appeared in Netflix's worldwide top ten for English-language series for three weeks. It reached second place and recorded 6.2 million views during its first complete week of availability. Those figures suggest that the comedy attracted considerable initial attention, although the report characterizes its performance as insufficiently exceptional relative to its expense.

The production was reportedly among the streaming service's most expensive comedies, with Ferrell receiving a seven-figure salary per episode. No exact production budget is provided, so the public viewing figures cannot establish the show's profitability on their own. The report places the decision within Netflix's broader practice of assessing performance against costs.

Critical and audience reactions also differed. At the time of the report, The Hawk held a 33 percent critics' score and a 65 percent audience score on Rotten Tomatoes. The gap suggests that viewers were more receptive than reviewers, but neither measure provides a complete explanation for the cancellation.

## A golfer refusing to give up

Ferrell played Lonnie Hawkins, a former world-leading golfer whose ambitions have outlasted his peak competitive years. Lonnie remains determined to win the major championship he needs to complete a career Grand Slam, even as his former wife and his successful golfing son Lance recognize that his best days may be behind him.

The cast included Molly Shannon, Jimmy Tatro, Fortune Feimster, Luke Wilson, Chris Parnell, Katelyn Tarver and David Hornsby. Ferrell developed the series with Harper Steele and Chris Henchy.

## Ferrell's Netflix projects continue

The cancellation does not end Ferrell's professional relationship with the streaming service. Through Gloria Sanchez Productions, he remains involved as an executive producer on upcoming Netflix projects including All the Rage, Prep and Nikki Glaser's first scripted series.

For viewers, The Hawk's fate is another reminder that a prominent position on a streaming chart does not necessarily guarantee renewal. The reported production costs provide important context, while the absence of a published budget means the precise financial calculation remains unknown.
